title: 9. Both Sides of the Aisle, Likely Outcomes & No-FOMO Action Plan

epigraph.quote: An investment thesis is not complete until you have argued the opposite side harder than your opponent, priced the base rates of failure, and written down the exact price at which you will act—or walk away.
epigraph.author: Portfolio Risk Committee

web_blocks.html: We now combine our Pass 1 audit with live valuation and Stage 2 charts. Both sides carry real proof. Bulls cite 28.7% H1 FY27 EBITDA margins, >28% ex-cash ROCE, ₹933 Cr cash, zero long-term debt, and the Q3 FY27 TPU line [24][25][33]. Bears cite 51% US sales, ~30% single-buyer share [2], and 149 inventory days [1]. Pass 1 added two more bear points. First, DGTR found under 25% total Indian PPF share and CY24 domestic PPF losses under 200%–300% Chinese undercutting, while Finance Ministry ADD enactment stays unverified [29][30]. Second, FY26 notes flag component auditors on foreign units (~36% of sales) and ₹215.74 Cr in contingencies [31].

book_paragraphs: Every institutional underwriting dossier must culminate at a clear decision table where the Bull and Bear cases are tested head-to-head and translated into exact rupee triggers. Across eight chapters, we audited Garware Hi-Tech Films from its Waluj polymer reactors and Lubrizol TPU extrusion line to its FY26 audit footnotes and multi-timeframe weekly, daily, and four-hour charts. Now we decide what to do with both our existing tracking share and our marginal cash.

The Bull case is concrete and cash-backed. Eighty-six percent of H1 FY27 revenue came from value-added specialty films—51% Sun Control Films and 24% Paint Protection Films—lifting H1 EBITDA margins to 28.7% and ex-cash ROCE above 28%. With ₹933 crore in cash and liquid investments, zero long-term debt, AA/AA- credit ratings from ICRA and CARE, ten straight years of positive free cash flow, and India's first Lubrizol-partnered TPU extrusion line commissioning in Q3 FY27, Garware has built a durable vertical cost moat.

The Bear case is equally tangible, and our Pass 1 blind-spot audit sharpened it further. Exports generate roughly 80% of revenue, half in the United States and roughly 30% tied to a single US customer—a concentration that stalled FY26 growth to 0.5% during the August 2025 US tariff shock and pushed inventory to 149 days. In India, DGTR's June 2026 Final Findings revealed that Garware held less than 25% total domestic PPF market share and incurred domestic PPF losses in CY2024 under 200% to 300% Chinese price undercutting, while Finance Ministry Customs notification of the recommended anti-dumping duty remains unverified as of November 2026. Meanwhile, FY26 footnotes highlight component-auditor reliance on two foreign subsidiaries generating 36% of consolidated revenue and ₹215.74 crore in contingent liabilities and commitments, including an unprovided ₹18.37 crore disputed tax demand.

Balancing both sides, Garware Hi-Tech Films retains its COMPOUNDER_PASS business quality grade with KPI health at PASS_WITH_WATCH and conviction capped at Tier 2. On price, however, the verified November 23 close of ₹7,895.00 sits at 43.0 times trailing earnings and +8.76% above the 10-week EMA, offering only 1.13-to-1 reward-to-risk to our ₹9,300 base target against our ratcheted ₹6,650 stop. Even after the live November 25 pullback to ₹7,628.00, the four-hour chart has not turned up.

Our dual verdict is therefore disciplined and unambiguous. For new capital, the verdict is WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT: do not chase ₹7,895.00 or buy an unconfirmed falling four-hour bar; wait for stabilization inside ₹7,250 to ₹7,650, where our ₹9,300 base target delivers an earned 1.65-to-1 asymmetry at the top of the band. For existing holdings, your Zerodha account now holds 1 tracking share of GRWRHITECH at ₹7,781.40 average cost (0.19% portfolio weight, +1.46% unrealized gain at ₹7,895.00). Our holding action is HOLD_WITH_HARD_STOP with zero shares to sell today, paired with an upward-only stop-loss ratchet from ₹6,520 to ₹6,650 via a Zerodha GTT sell order.

For the next ₹100,000 unit of Zerodha cash (from ₹15.39 lakh available as of November 23), we compare cash against shortlist peer Titan and outside peer Cosmo First. Titan closed at ₹4,680.00 near its ₹4,550–₹4,696 support band, but currently sits in Stage 3 with six distribution days and negative 63-day relative strength. Cosmo First trades cheaply at 9.3 times earnings, yet its 11.2% ROCE and breakdown below its 50-day and 30-week moving averages make it structurally inferior. Accordingly, we keep 100% of our marginal cash in dry powder until Garware confirms support inside ₹7,250 to ₹7,650.

Over the next two quarters, your monitoring checklist has four items: verify Q3 FY27 Lubrizol TPU commissioning and early margin uplift; confirm inventory days normalize below 130 alongside the final ₹30 crore US tariff refund; watch for official Finance Ministry Customs notification on Chinese TPU PPF anti-dumping duties; and verify clean audit continuity across overseas subsidiaries. Keep your ₹6,650 GTT active on the starter share, wait patiently for 4-hour confirmation in ₹7,250–₹7,650, and let disciplined risk geometry do the heavy lifting.

Remember why capping Garware at Tier 2 conviction matters even though the business earned a clean COMPOUNDER_PASS. Fifty-one percent geographic exposure to the United States and roughly 30% revenue concentration in a single customer mean an external policy shock can arrive without warning. By sizing the eventual position in two disciplined tranches inside ₹7,250 to ₹7,650 and anchoring every share to our upward-ratcheted ₹6,650 stop, we give ourselves full participation in Garware's 28%-plus ex-cash ROCE compounding engine while ensuring no single tariff headline can impair the portfolio.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: Holding a 1-share tracking starter keeps you anchored to a great compounder without violating risk discipline. Ratchet your GTT stop upward to ₹6,650 behind the rising 30-week SMA, keep 100% of marginal cash dry, and scale only when ₹7,250–₹7,650 holds on the 4-hour chart.
